reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) from the same paper directly supports the formation, thickness, composition, friction coefficient (~0.09), and order-of-magnitude wear reduction for the (TiNbZr)75Ag25 alloy in ambient air. However, the hypothesis extends the effective temperature range to 600 °C, which is not mentioned in the cited passages, leaving that premise unsupported.
premises: Adding ~25 at.% Ag to a TiNbZr alloy forms a ~400 nm thick amorphous-crystalline oxide nanocomposite tribolayer during dry sliding in air
This tribolayer reduces the friction coefficient to ~0.09
This tribolayer reduces the wear rate by an order of magnitude (or two orders) relative to the Ag-free alloy
The mechanism involves Ag promoting oxidation and the positive enthalpy of mixing with Nb driving Ag nanocrystal nucleation
The effect is effective from room temperature up to ~600 °C in oxygen-rich environments
